title: Minimal diagnoses
description: Reiter's faulty full adder: sets of broken gates that explain the observed outputs while no proper subset does, that is, models of the circuit that are minimal in the broken gates with the wires varying (circumscription; Pi-2-complete in general, Eiter and Gottlob). The abstraction guesses broken gates and wire values with the suspect gate broken, and the check looks for an explanation with fewer broken gates. The circuit rules are written once, with a world argument, and used by both solvers.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: Derived facts about the circuit. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% The instance (its facts) is in the Instances tab.
% gate(Name, Kind, Input1, Input2, Output), wire(X), obs(X,Value); the constant
% suspect names a gate.
part(G) :- gate(G,_,_,_,_).

fragments.name: circuit
fragments.description: The behaviour of the circuit in a world; used by solver A and by solver C.
fragments.text:
% How the circuit behaves in a world W. Solver A uses the world "now" (the candidate),
% solver C the world "alt" (the counterexample); the rules are written once.
% on(W,X): wire X carries 1 in world W.  broken(W,G): gate G is assumed faulty there.
out(W,G) :- gate(G,and,X,Y,_), on(W,X), on(W,Y).
out(W,G) :- gate(G,or,X,_,_), on(W,X).
out(W,G) :- gate(G,or,_,Y,_), on(W,Y).
out(W,G) :- gate(G,xor,X,Y,_), on(W,X), not on(W,Y).
out(W,G) :- gate(G,xor,X,Y,_), on(W,Y), not on(W,X).
% A gate that is not broken computes its function; a broken gate may output anything.
:- world(W), gate(G,_,_,_,Z), not broken(W,G), on(W,Z), not out(W,G).
:- world(W), gate(G,_,_,_,Z), not broken(W,G), not on(W,Z), out(W,G).
% The observations hold.
:- world(W), obs(X,1), not on(W,X).
:- world(W), obs(X,0), on(W,X).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): broken gates and wire values that fit the observations.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a set of broken gates and a value for every wire that fit the
% observations (the circuit fragment sees to that for the world "now").
world(now).
{ broken(now,G) } :- part(G).
{ on(now,X) } :- wire(X).
% Is the suspect gate part of a minimal diagnosis? (Each instance sets the constant.)
:- not broken(now,suspect).
#show.
#show broken(G) : broken(now,G).
#show on(X) : on(now,X).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: which gates the candidate breaks. The wire values stay private to solver A.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for an explanation that breaks fewer gates (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: the observations can also be explained in a world "alt" in which a
% proper subset of the candidate's gates is broken. The wires may take other values.
world(alt).
{ broken(alt,G) } :- broken(now,G).
{ on(alt,X) } :- wire(X).
mended(G) :- broken(now,G), not broken(alt,G).
fewer :- mended(G).
:- not fewer.
#show.
#show broken(G) : broken(alt,G).

% The smaller explanation refutes every candidate that breaks its gates and at least
% one more. Mark its gates and, as a witness, the first gate it mends.
relevant(broken(now,G)) :- broken(alt,G).
relevant(broken(now,G)) :- mended(G), not mended(H) : part(H), H < G.

fragments.name: check_all_mended
fragments.description: The check of the variant all-mended: every mended gate is blamed, not only the first.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: the observations can also be explained in a world "alt" in which a
% proper subset of the candidate's gates is broken. The wires may take other values.
world(alt).
{ broken(alt,G) } :- broken(now,G).
{ on(alt,X) } :- wire(X).
mended(G) :- broken(now,G), not broken(alt,G).
fewer :- mended(G).
:- not fewer.
#show.
#show broken(G) : broken(alt,G).

% The smaller explanation refutes every candidate that breaks its gates and at least
% one more. Mark its gates and all the gates it mends (weaker than naming the first one,
% still sound).
relevant(broken(now,G)) :- broken(alt,G).
relevant(broken(now,G)) :- mended(G).

fragments.name: check_small
fragments.description: The check of the variant smallest: a smaller explanation with as few broken gates as possible, so the clause is short.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: the observations can also be explained in a world "alt" in which a
% proper subset of the candidate's gates is broken. The wires may take other values.
world(alt).
{ broken(alt,G) } :- broken(now,G).
{ on(alt,X) } :- wire(X).
mended(G) :- broken(now,G), not broken(alt,G).
fewer :- mended(G).
:- not fewer.
#show.
#show broken(G) : broken(alt,G).
% The smallest refinement (variant smallest): as few broken gates in alt as possible.
#minimize { 1,G : broken(alt,G) }.

% The smaller explanation refutes every candidate that breaks its gates and at least
% one more. Mark its gates and, as a witness, the first gate it mends.
relevant(broken(now,G)) :- broken(alt,G).
relevant(broken(now,G)) :- mended(G), not mended(H) : part(H), H < G.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + circuit + abstraction
solver C = shared + circuit + check     options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

instances.facts:
% A full adder: gate(Name, Kind, Input1, Input2, Output).
gate(x1,xor,a,b,p).
gate(x2,xor,p,c,s).
gate(a1,and,a,b,q).
gate(a2,and,p,c,r).
gate(o1,or,q,r,co).
wire(a;b;c;p;q;r;s;co).
% Observed: with inputs a = 1, b = 0, c = 1 the adder shows sum s = 1 and carry co = 0
% (it should show s = 0 and co = 1).
obs(a,1). obs(b,0). obs(c,1). obs(s,1). obs(co,0).
% Is gate x2 part of a minimal diagnosis?

% The full adder showing the right answer (1 + 0 + 1 = 10): the only minimal
% diagnosis is the empty one, so no minimal diagnosis blames x2.
% A full adder: gate(Name, Kind, Input1, Input2, Output).
gate(x1,xor,a,b,p).
gate(x2,xor,p,c,s).
gate(a1,and,a,b,q).
gate(a2,and,p,c,r).
gate(o1,or,q,r,co).
wire(a;b;c;p;q;r;s;co).
obs(a,1). obs(b,0). obs(c,1). obs(s,0). obs(co,1).

% A 2-bit ripple-carry adder (two full adders; c1 carries from bit 0 to bit 1).
gate(x1,xor,a0,b0,p0). gate(x2,xor,p0,c0,s0). gate(a1,and,a0,b0,q0).
gate(a2,and,p0,c0,r0). gate(o1,or,q0,r0,c1).
gate(x3,xor,a1,b1,p1). gate(x4,xor,p1,c1,s1). gate(a3,and,a1,b1,q1).
gate(a4,and,p1,c1,r1). gate(o2,or,q1,r1,c2).
wire(a0;b0;c0;p0;s0;q0;r0;c1;a1;b1;p1;s1;q1;r1;c2).
% Observed: 01 + 11 with carry-in 0 shows s1 s0 = 10 and carry c2 = 0
% (it should show 00 and carry 1).
obs(a0,1). obs(b0,1). obs(c0,0). obs(a1,0). obs(b1,1). obs(s0,0). obs(s1,1). obs(c2,0).
% Is gate x4 part of a minimal diagnosis?

generators.name: circuit-random
generators.description: A random circuit: k inputs and g gates (and, or, xor), each reading two different earlier wires; random input values, the unused outputs observed and the last output flipped. Set the constant suspect to a gate number (k+1 .. k+g).
generators.text:
% circuit-random: wires 1..k are inputs, gate I (k < I <= k+g) is an and, or or xor gate
% whose output is wire I and whose two inputs are two different earlier wires. The inputs
% get random values; every input and every unused output is observed, with the output of
% the last gate flipped (one fault shows). Set the constant suspect to a gate number.
input(1..k).
wire(1..k+g).
kind(I,@int(1,3,kind,I)) :- I = k+1..k+g.
in1(I,@int(1,I-1,in1,I)) :- I = k+1..k+g.
in2(I,(X+@int(0,I-3,gap,I))\(I-1)+1) :- in1(I,X).
gate(I,and,X,Y,I) :- kind(I,1), in1(I,X), in2(I,Y).
gate(I,or,X,Y,I) :- kind(I,2), in1(I,X), in2(I,Y).
gate(I,xor,X,Y,I) :- kind(I,3), in1(I,X), in2(I,Y).
on(I) :- input(I), @flip(500,value,I) = 1.
on(I) :- gate(I,and,X,Y,I), on(X), on(Y).
on(I) :- gate(I,or,X,Y,I), on(X).
on(I) :- gate(I,or,X,Y,I), on(Y).
on(I) :- gate(I,xor,X,Y,I), on(X), not on(Y).
on(I) :- gate(I,xor,X,Y,I), on(Y), not on(X).
used(X) :- in1(I,X).
used(X) :- in2(I,X).
shown(I) :- input(I).
shown(I) :- I = k+1..k+g-1, not used(I).
obs(I,1) :- shown(I), on(I).
obs(I,0) :- shown(I), not on(I).
obs(k+g,0) :- on(k+g).
obs(k+g,1) :- not on(k+g).
#show gate/5.  #show wire/1.  #show obs/2.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + circuit + abstraction
solver C = shared + circuit + check     options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The blocking loop: each refuted candidate is ruled out on its own.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + circuit + abstraction
solver C = shared + circuit + check     options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three counterexamples per candidate, one clause each.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + circuit + abstraction
solver C = shared + circuit + check     options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The smallest refinement: an optimal counterexample (check_small minimises the
# atoms that relevant/1 blames), so its clause is as short as possible.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M), optimal)
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + circuit + abstraction
solver C = shared + circuit + check     options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)
